wave_title: Direct follow-up to the prior generation's own recorded next step: 'cycle detection / fixed-point resolution (cycle.rs) -- likely the concrete mechanism behind R5's own fixed-point naming ... flagged as the natural next slice of THIS donor's own census'. Confirmed correct on inspection: cycle.rs opens with a module doc comment explicitly titled around fixed-point iteration, read in full before any other claim was made.
priority_classification: semantic preservation / roadmap advancement -- continuing the same donor-research thread the prior generation opened, following its own explicitly recorded next step rather than starting a new, unrelated investigation.
key_finding: Salsa's cycle handling is a real Kleene-style fixed-point iteration with two subtleties easy to miss: (1) convergence requires BOTH the computed value AND its revision metadata (durability) to stabilize (execute.rs:792, `this_converged = value_converged && metadata_converged`) -- checking value equality alone, the obvious naive design, would be unsound against the companion genome record's own shallow-verification optimization; (2) finality propagates LAZILY, not eagerly -- only the cycle head is marked final the moment it converges; every other query in the cycle keeps its provisional status until the NEXT time it is actually read, at which point the reader checks whether all of ITS OWN cycle heads are now final. A hard MAX_ITERATIONS=200 safety bound (cycle.rs:52) acknowledges the mechanism cannot itself prove a user-supplied recovery function is well-behaved.
method: read cycle.rs's module doc comment in full (lines 1-42) before reading any code, confirming the hypothesis from the prior generation before investigating further; then read the actual convergence-checking code in function/execute.rs (lines 215-295, 764-833) to verify the doc comment's own prose claims against the real implementation, not accepting the doc comment alone as sufficient evidence (the same discipline this session applies to its own R4 walker doc comments, applied here to a donor's documentation instead).
